body:
I don't think it's correct to substitute "control point" for every existing usage of "vertex". There are multiple kinds of points, and this existing description clearly implies a difference between control points and "vertices". So "vertices" and "control points" are not the same.

Substituting only "point" for "vertex" might also be misleading, since in the inspector for a Curve2D, you have an array of `Point`s which each contain a `Position` and an `In` and/or an `Out`.

![Godot_v4 3-stable_mono_win64_KuRzoegbFq](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c46e663-36d8-418f-b191-eb03697c46d5)

I'm not familiar enough with Curve2D to suggest a correct replacement for the "vertex" term, though.

body:
Curve2D and Curve3D use the [bezier_interpolate()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector2.html#class-vector2-method-bezier-interpolate) function of Vector2 and Vector3.
The description of the function also uses the term "control points" and links to a [Bézier curve article on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve) where it's used, too. I couldn't find the term "vertex" in this context and think "control point" is the correct replacement.

Right, "control point" might be a fine substitute for some of these usages. But look at the existing description in this case:
> Returns the position of the control point leading out of the vertex [param idx]...

And compare it to your changed version:
> Returns the position of the control point leading out of the control point [param idx]...

The term "control point" is already used. But it's not used for every kind of point, because the existing description draws a distinction between "control points" and "vertices". So at the very least in this case, I'm not sure if substituting "control point" for "vertex" is correct. And in all the other changed cases, you should be careful you're not introducing a subtle error.

Maybe I'm repeating the exact same sentiment as @tetrapod00, but [all points of a curve are referred to as "control points"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve#:~:text=The%20points%20Pi%20are,polygon%20contains%20the%20B%C3%A9zier%20curve.). However, it seems like the existing descriptions hint that only `in` and `out` should be named that way, which is not accurate as the `position` is a control point, too.

I think repeating the same two words twice is confusing, but I have little suggestions. Perhaps `set_point_in` and similar should not repeat "control" twice.

body:
The problem might run deeper, actually. The [class description](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_curve2d.html#description) for Curve2D describes it as "a Bézier curve in 2D space". But is that accurate? You can (manually) change the control points coming out of each "Point"/"vertex" so that some "vertices" are sharp:

![Godot_v4 3-stable_mono_win64_83PMOSIntD](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c833321-cce7-467c-9a68-dd75eb39abc0)

To me, this looks more like a [Composite Bezier Curve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composite_B%C3%A9zier_curve) as defined by Wikipedia, which is a *series* of individual Bezier curves. In that case, "vertex" is not a totally unused term, going by Wikipedia:
> A béziergon (also called bézigon) is a closed path composed of [Bézier curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve). It is similar to a [polygon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon) in that it connects a set of [vertices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertex_(geometry)) by lines, but whereas in polygons the vertices are connected by straight lines, in a béziergon the vertices are connected by Bézier curves.

The method description for [add_point()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_curve2d.html#class-curve2d-method-add-point) calls the "vertices" simply "points", which have a "position" and "control points":
> Adds a point with the specified `position` relative to the curve's own position, with control points `in` and `out`. Appends the new point at the end of the point list.

That `position` *will* be used as a control point for the individual Bezier curves which connect the "points" or "vertices". But currently there is a distinction drawn between that control point, and the `in` and `out` control points, because they are edited in different ways. The Curve2D class is *not* simply a list of control points which make a single Bezier curve. I don't think it makes sense to call everything here a control point because you lose some clarity.

But, I really don't have a lot of experience with curves and the precise terminology, though.

body:
A Composite Bezier Curve is continuous according to the Wikipedia site, but it appears to be close to what we have.

Looking at the [code](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2582793d408ade0b6ed42f913ae33e7da5fb9184/scene/resources/curve.cpp#L822), a Curve2D is sampled with 4 points like a cubic Bezier curve. While following this hint, I found this information about [specific cases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve#Specific_cases):

> A Bézier curve is defined by a [set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_(mathematics)) of [control points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Control_point_(mathematics)) P0 through Pn, where n is called the order of the curve (n = 1 for linear, 2 for quadratic, 3 for cubic, etc.). The first and last control points are always the endpoints of the curve; however, the intermediate control points generally do not lie on the curve. The sums in the following sections are to be understood as [affine combinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_space#Affine_combinations_and_barycenter) – that is, the coefficients sum to 1.

Is this what we have in Godot, using "control points"?

I'm at a loss to be honest...
